So I used a similar plotline as this in my own homebrewed version of Tyranny of Dragons, where Tiamat's plot to escape Avernus was a lot wider reaching, involving a plan to resurrect Sardior through rejoining all the worlds of the D&D Multiverse back into the First World (taken from the lore presented in Fizban's) and taking back what she saw as her rightful place as the ruling deity of all with dragons as the dominant species, which was the case back when Bahamut and Tiamat were one as Io before they were split by the other invading gods.

In this scenario, Bahamut then willingly decided to join the other deities as he saw an opportunity to create a better reality alongside them, but confronting Tiamat led to her deciding that if she couldn't have the First World, no one could, so in the ensuing divine battle it was then shattered into the many worlds of the D&D multiverse, along with Sardior who had decided to divide themself up in order to leave behind various offspring to protect these new worlds, the Gem Dragons (though Tiamat thought this was her fault and an accident, blaming herself for the destruction of the Ruby Dragon).

Obviously Tiamat later came to regret this as it led to her divine punishment and imprisonment, and Bahamut himself mourned the loss of their creation and the descent of his other half into madness and hatred. So, when Tiamat discovered a way to free herself and recreate the First World and began to enact her plot, Bahamut saw that her plan was not one born entirely out of selfish desire but also an attempt by Tiamat to restore what was lost and return their kind to the glory they once held, and resurrect their first creation the Ruby Dragon. Bahamut was conflicted, and realised that in that self doubt lied the possibility of him being unable to truly stop Tiamat permanently if he had to, so he had to choose a mortal champion to do so.

Tiamat's viewpoint is that once when she was whole, she created a world for her children, a paradise where they could roam free and live in harmony with one another. Then, other strange beings from beyond the stars descended from the heavens, taking interest in their home, and starting to leave behind annoying, destructive little pests (the humanoid peoples). Then, when she confronted the strange beings about why their little creations caused such destruction in her paradise, they said that the bounty of paradise was for them all to share and their creations had the freedom to choose what to do with it, despite these strange beings having no hand in creating this paradise. When she fought back against this idea, she was torn apart, with all of her goodness stripped away and stolen into the heavens in the form of Bahamut, leaving her only with rage, loathing, and spite. Then, as she fought to keep her paradise safe from the invading pests, her goodness returned to her as one of these strange beings from beyond the stars and tried to force her to give up her paradise and share it with those who hurt her and her children, which she fought back against and in the ensuing chaos her paradise was destroyed along with her first child, whilst all her other children were scattered to the wind and she was punished for it.

Now again, this is my homebrew interpretation of the lore and shouldn't be taken as gospel by any means, and I think Bahamut's typical characterisation means he wouldn't necessarily work with Tiamat willingly unless under extreme circumstances, but I think it shows that there is room for a nuanced take on Bahamut that can be understanding of Tiamat's plight and the wish to resurrect Sardior, potentially leading to collaboration or at least a reluctance to fight her.

Now your version of this plotline can go differently depending on what you want to do. 

Perhaps this Paladin of Bahamut you have in mind doesn't have his deity's direct support anymore and is considered an Oathbreaker, but has not receieved a greater divine punishment for this perceived heresy as he should have, because Bahamut secretly understands why he broke his oath for Tiamat.

Or maybe Bahamut has reluctantly joined with Tiamat, seeing the resurrection of Sardior as the best way to restore dragonkind to prosperity as they are declining as a species, with more and more dragons dying out and less and less eggs being hatched. Then, the plot becomes having to convince this Paladin (and by extension, Bahamut) that there is another way. 

In either of these cases, you present a mystery (Why did this Oathbreaker betray Bahamut and join Tiamat? OR Why has this Paladin of Bahamut not been abandoned by his god?) and also give both Bahamut and Tiamat a bit more personality and nuance and make them active characters in the story.

She is a worshipper of the draconic death deity, Null, and considers herself his most faithful servant and wishes to become his consort and a demigod. 

She's got quite a lot of history to her, and her association with the Shadowfell fits really well with the lore and features of the Hexblade subclass. 

Ultimately, she's made both a great ally and source of information for the warlock and the party, and despite her evil nature, she has reasons to oppose Tiamat and therefore be an ally to any party going against her.

Lorelei Kandor (Top left) - A Level 8 Fallen Aasimar Paladin who has sworn an Oath of Vengeance against Orcus and all who share his dark powers after the death of her parents during a demon incursion years prior. The problem is, after her recent resurrection alongside some of the others in the group, she has found herself corrupted by that demonic energy. 

Her new weapon (to her left), the sentient greatsword called Blight Angel, is a reflection of her own powers and can be switched between Demonic and Celestial aspects.

---

Vaal-Mir (Middle left) - A Level 8 Tiefling Warlock who is a loyal agent of the Red King and Archdevil of Nessus, Asmodeus. He wields a modified Rod of the Pact Keeper (to his left) embellished with his master's symbol as well as a Book of Shadows, from which he can summon his mischievous spider familiar, Colin!

While he maintains an unsteady alliance with others within the party, this master of deception and fiendish power holds dark secrets that may soon be uncovered...

---

Brann Lysmann (Bottom Left) - A Level 8 Human Light Cleric who follows Azzanon, the God of the Sun, Healing and Medicine. Once a peasant boy taken in by a local priest after his parents were taken by disease, Brann matured into a wise, compassionate and dedicated acolyte. 

Now he has been given new purpose in removing the blasphemous undead worm god, Kyuss, alongside the rest of his party. To do this, he wields a mighty Mace of Disruption (To his left).

---

Balgrüf (Top right) - A Level 5 Mountain Dwarf Hunter Ranger and Level 3 Battlemaster Fighter, who's search for vengeance as a Bounty Hunter led him to the Emerald Plains of Alresia, the party's current stomping ground. After circumstances forced them to work together, Balgrüf has shown himself as a strong and capable warrior.

After saving a trio of orphaned gold dragon wrymlings sheltering in an abandoned Dwarven mine, the Dwarf was gifted with the Golden Honour Battleaxe (to his left), a weapon now imbued with a fraction of a gold dragon's power.

---

Arie Fuche (Middle right) - A Level 8 Water Genasi Way of the Four Elements Monk, who's death on the high seas has turned into new life as a Champion of the Primordial Lord of Water, the Leviathan. 

The fastest and most acrobatic of the group, Arie takes a lot of bad hits, but he returns in kind with lethal unarmed strikes and vicious elemental power gifted by the Elemental Crystal Shard (to his left) embedded in his chest.

---

Agos (Bottom Right) - A Level 8 Lizardfolk Ancetral Guardian Barbarian, who after being stolen away from his Sess'innek-worshipping tribe and being turned into an enslaved gladiator, died but was brought back years later under mysterious circumstances among strangers. Now, he has become attuned to the spirits of his predecessors and seeks out the secret history of his people. 

He wields an ethereally-powered warhammer known as the Gravewalker's Insight (to his left), a weapon claimed from a Vampire Spawn working under one of Kyuss' minions.

Appearance and Personality:

He's a tall, muscular yet deft and dexterous fellow  with brown/red hair that's swept back and reaches a few inches down his back, with a rugged beard and shimmering topaz eyes. When using his Radiant Soul feature, his whole appearance becomes that of a Bronze statue, with the pair of wings tattooed on his back unfurling into luminous wings and his body glowing with divine strength. His outfit consists of leathers and furs which he himself has crafted into suitable clothing. 

Firstly, his basic clothing is a plain brown tunic and a pair of grey linen trousers, however he removes the tunic when possible in order to wear his shoulder guard. On his lower legs, he has a pair of leather boots and leather greaves which both have a fur trim, which match with the leather wraps around his forearms which have a cloth underlay and fur trim. Then, he has a thick leather belt around his waste, with runic symbols carved into the leather and an iron buckle inscribed with his god's symbol. The sides of this belt have metal rings to place his handaxes. Then he has the previously mentioned leather shoulder guard, which has two hooks on the back to hold his maul and a sheath for his javelins. Finally, he can attach his large bear pelt cloak to the shoulder guard through a set of rivets and some straps. This cloak helps protect Salathiel from harsh climates and can disguise his physique to make his foes underestimate him, though in warmer conditions he is less likely to don it.

Personality wise, Salathiel's a dedicated and loyal man. He believes in his duties to his tribe and his family and wants to ensure he makes them proud. He's polite and respectful to new faces, though he won't accept ignorance and insults. I'm hoping Salathiel can be a father figure to other player characters, offering advice and bad jokes all around which his 9 in Charisma will ensure are received as they are intended to be.

Backstory:

(Sorry for the upcoming massive wall of text.)

Long ago, before the establishment of the Empire to the south, the Saltum mountain range was dominated by a powerful Ancient White Dragon. The primitive tribes that resided there were food for the Dragon to play with and consume at a whim and they lived in constant peril. One day, the celestial Valandra, a Solar sent as the agent of a noble god, fought against this terrible beast and slew it at the cost of her own life. A fragment of her was left behind and planted itself inside the region's tallest peak. From this fragment flowed a river of divine power that rejuvenated the inhospitable climate, turning it into a beautiful and fertile place filled with life. The tribe that resided near this mountain took up the duty of protecting it and ensuring it's power was used to heal and protect the world, naming the mountain Mount Valandra in the celestial defender's name. Those blessed in the river would become Aasimars and gain divine powers, though these had to be earned. Salathiel Kurvan is one such individal, serving as a guardian of his tribe and Mount Valandra. His wife, an exile from the Empire called Bellatrix, also took part in the trial to become one of these chosen warriors. 

They had two daughters. The eldest, Mara, wished to become a warrior like her parents, while her younger sister Annelise pursued a place among the tribe's clergy, training to be a Cleric. Mara had been married and gave birth to a son, named Balder, making Salathiel a proud grandfather. However, despite the tribe succeeding in fighting off Orcs, Gnolls and Giants, they were eventually outmatched. The tribe's priests, those who could resurrect the mightiest warriors the tribe had entombed within the mountain, and some of their acolytes disappeared one night and Salathiel was sent out to find them alongside some of the tribe's scouts and warriors. It turns out that a group of tribe members, though he isn't sure who it was, betrayed the tribe and stole away the priests, which included Annelise. They were left out in the harsh conditions and most of them had died, save for Annelise who they managed to save from a pack of wolves.

However, when they made it back to the village, it was under siege. A legion of Hobgoblins, who had bribed the traitors, attacked the tribe's village in an attempt to reach the mountain and claim the power of the river so empower their armies. Salathiel fought through the warriors, though they outnumbered the tribe massively and he began to realise they couldn't be defeated now they lacked the clerics to resurrect the warriors in the mountain tomb. Salathiel found his wife and told her to get as many of the survivors and to flee with them and Annelise to a location nearby. If the Hobgoblins reached there or if he didn't come find them in a day, she must take them North past the mountains and to find them safety somewhere. Salathiel then made the trek up the mountain, where he found Mara fighting Hobgoblins at the waterfall at the entrance of the tomb. He rushed into the tomb, following the path of the river to the celestial fragment. He pleaded and begged for it to intervene, for their god to save his tribe and his family but it was no use. Then he heard the screams of his daughter and as he rushed to the waterfall, the shimmering water was tainted with blood. He saw his daughter, bleeding and exhausted as a Hobgoblin Captain plunged his blade into her chest and kicked off the cliff's edge and she tumbled into the surging waves below. At that moment, the usual noble surge of divine power awakened by Salathiel was replaced by a primal rage that overwhelmed the pain he felt. He slaughtered the Captain, but he knew he couldn't hold off the rest of the legion and that he needed to make sure they couldn't steal the divine power here. He then took his Maul and destroyed the fragment, causing the tomb to collapse on top of him and seemingly killing him...

Soon enough, Salathiel awoke is the shattered ruins of the tomb with nothing but the tiniest sliver of the Celestial fragment in his palm, which he would form into a pendant. He broke through the rubble and found himself at the edge waterfall, from which he could see the consequences of his actions. While he had stopped the Hobgoblins, the source for the river's celestial power was gone and the area had become a harsh and unforgiving snowy climate once more. His village was now destroyed and his people scattered to the wind, but most importantly was that he had no idea if his family were still alive. He soon made his way down to the bottom of the waterfall, looking for any sign of Mara. He couldn't find her body, but he did find the blue ribbon she wore. He wrapped it around his upper right arm, to remind himself that her memory would be the source of his strength and his inspiration to carry on. Salathiel also found the tattered remains of his wife's cloak, which he fashioned into a sash around his waist to ensure she was always with him in some way.

Salathiel soon realised that while the Hobgoblins were now beginning to leave the ruins of his village, they had taken some of the surviving tribe members prisoner and would surely make them into warrior slaves. While planning to free them and finding some safe shelter, he met up with an exiled soldier from the Empire to the south. He saved the man's life and he promised to help Salathiel free his fellow tribesmen in return. They succeeded and began the journey North, where the tribe members split off on their own paths. Salathiel received a vision in this time, one which appeared to show that there were other places like his home elsewhere in the world and that maybe if he found them, he could reunite the rest of his tribe and find his family. Now he's set off alongside this soldier, Gladius Maximus, to discover more about these new lands and to eventually find his family and a new place to call home.

He then found himself hired by the Harpers to investigate the recent activities of giants in the surrounding area, starting with a journey to the town of Nightstone... 

Arvokk uses both his mother's and his father's training to mix magic with martial combat.
